subject: mathematics
question_text: Show that the determinant with rows (b+c, c+a, a+b), (c+a, a+b, b+c) and (a+b, b+c, c+a) is equal to twice the determinant with rows (a, b, c), (b, c, a) and (c, a, b).

mark_split.label: Take −1 from R₂ and R₃ to finish

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.26 — LAQ chapter 3 Matrices, answer 17, the last determinant proof before the chapter turns to solving systems. The mark split is PRINTED in that book's margin as 1+1+1+2+1+1 across the six working lines — a sourced split, and the one this answer book uses as the model for the two questions on book p.24 where no split is printed. The book's own margin note reads 'I was asked TWICE', matching the two printed appearances (AP 15,16). Star rank is the CHAPTER's ★★★, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section C runs Q18-Q24 at 7 marks each, answer any 5 of 7. Re-cut to the 8-mark Section-C form of the 2026-27 pattern (TGBIE model paper w.e.f. 2026-27): the extra mark goes to the "Take −1 from R₂ and R₃ to finish" step.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — this one uses the same row-adding move twice, so say where each one goes and what happens in between.

steps.label: Write the determinant
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Note that the right-hand side is a determinant, not a number — so the job is to TRANSFORM this one into that one, not to evaluate anything.
steps.memory_tip: The right-hand side is a DETERMINANT, not a number — the job is to transform, not to evaluate.

lines.text: \Delta = \begin{vmatrix} b+c & c+a & a+b \\ c+a & a+b & b+c \\ a+b & b+c & c+a \end{vmatrix}

recall.must_convey: That the working starts from the given determinant. Naming it is full credit.
accept: write the given determinant first
take delta as the determinant of b plus c c plus a a plus b
start with the LHS determinant
modata ichina determinant rasta
write down the determinant on the left side

steps.why: The answer is another determinant with a 2 in front. That tells you the proof ends by reshaping, not by expanding — so never expand this one.
common_mistakes: Expanding both sides and trying to match the results.
Reading the right-hand side as a number.

steps.label: Add all three rows into R₁
steps.mark_note: Row sum and the common entry
steps.margin_note: The first two marks, one for the operation and one for doing the sum correctly. Down every column the three entries add to 2a+2b+2c — each of a, b and c appears exactly twice.
steps.memory_tip: Down every column the three entries add to 2a+2b+2c, since each letter appears twice.

lines.text: \Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 2(a{+}b{+}c) & 2(a{+}b{+}c) & 2(a{+}b{+}c) \\ c+a & a+b & b+c \\ a+b & b+c & c+a \end{vmatrix}

recall.must_convey: That rows 2 and 3 are added into row 1, and that every entry of the new top row is 2(a+b+c).
accept: add row two and row three into row one so the top row becomes two into a plus b plus c
apply R one plus R two plus R three and each entry of the first row is two a plus two b plus two c
sum the rows into the first row where every entry comes out the same
R1 ki R2 R3 kalipithe top row anni two into a plus b plus c avthai
each of a b and c appears twice so the sum is two a plus b plus c
reject: apply R one plus R two
heard_as: two a plus b plus c

steps.why: Each column holds b+c, c+a and a+b in some order. Adding them gives 2a+2b+2c whichever order they came in, which is why the operation works on all three columns at once.
common_mistakes: Writing a+b+c instead of 2(a+b+c) — count again, each letter appears twice.
Changing rows 2 and 3 as well; only row 1 is replaced.

steps.label: Take the 2 out
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Only the 2 comes out here, not the (a+b+c). Taking the whole bracket out as well would be wrong — the rows below still need it.
steps.memory_tip: Only the 2 comes out here, NOT the (a+b+c) — the rows below still need it.

lines.text: \Delta = 2\begin{vmatrix} a{+}b{+}c & a{+}b{+}c & a{+}b{+}c \\ c+a & a+b & b+c \\ a+b & b+c & c+a \end{vmatrix}

recall.must_convey: That the factor 2 is taken common out of row 1, leaving a+b+c in each entry of that row.
accept: take two common from the first row leaving a plus b plus c in each entry
pull the two outside the determinant
the factor two comes out and the top row is a plus b plus c three times
first row nunchi two common teeste a plus b plus c migulutundi
take only the two out and keep a plus b plus c inside
reject: take a plus b plus c common

steps.why: This 2 is the 2 in the answer. It comes out here and simply waits at the front while the rest of the determinant is reshaped.
common_mistakes: Taking 2(a+b+c) out and being left with a row of 1s that cannot recover the letters.
Forgetting the 2 entirely and finishing with the right determinant but no factor.

steps.label: Do R₂−R₁ and R₃−R₁
steps.margin_note: Two more marks. Subtracting the top row from each lower row leaves single negative letters — because (c+a) − (a+b+c) is just −b. Do all six entries the same way.
steps.memory_tip: Subtracting the top row leaves single negative letters: (c+a) − (a+b+c) is just −b.
lines: R₂ → R₂ − R₁ and R₃ → R₃ − R₁:
(c+a) − (a+b+c) = −b, and so on for each entry:

recall.must_convey: That row 1 is subtracted from rows 2 and 3, and that each resulting entry is a single negative letter — minus b, minus c, minus a and so on.
accept: subtract row one from row two and row three so each entry becomes a single negative letter
apply R two minus R one and R three minus R one leaving minus b minus c minus a in the second row
take the top row away from both lower rows and only single letters with minus signs are left
R2 minus R1 cheste minus b minus c minus a vasthundi
each entry becomes minus one letter because the rest cancels
reject: apply R two minus R one

steps.why: Every lower entry was a sum of two letters and the top row was the sum of all three. Subtracting leaves exactly the one letter that was missing, with a minus sign.
common_mistakes: Doing R₁ − R₂ and getting the letters positive but the top row destroyed.
Working out one entry and assuming the pattern rather than checking each.
Losing the 2 that is standing outside.

steps.label: Add the rows into R₁ again
steps.margin_note: Sixth mark, and the move students do not expect: the same operation is used a second time. Down column 1, (a+b+c) − b − c leaves a. Columns 2 and 3 leave b and c.
steps.memory_tip: The same operation a SECOND time — unexpected, but it is what rebuilds the target rows.
lines: R₁ → R₁ + R₂ + R₃ once more:
(a+b+c) − b − c = a,  and likewise b and c:

recall.must_convey: That the row-adding operation is applied a second time, and that the top row collapses from a+b+c to the single letters a, b, c.
accept: apply R one plus R two plus R three again so the top row becomes a b c
do the row sum a second time and a plus b plus c minus b minus c leaves a
add the rows into the first row once more to get single letters on top
malli R1 ki R2 R3 kalipithe top row a b c avthundi
the same operation is used twice and now the first row is just a b c

steps.why: The negative letters produced by the last step are exactly what is needed to cancel the surplus in the top row. That is why the same operation, repeated, does something completely different the second time.
common_mistakes: Assuming an operation can only be used once and getting stuck here.
Adding only one row instead of both.
Getting the cancellation backwards and leaving −a on top.

steps.label: Take −1 from R₂ and R₃
steps.margin_note: Last two marks. A −1 leaves each of the two lower rows, and (−1)(−1) = 1 — so the signs vanish and only the 2 is left in front, which is exactly what was to be shown.
steps.memory_tip: A −1 leaves each lower row, and (−1)(−1) = 1, so only the 2 survives in front.
lines: Taking −1 common from R₂ and from R₃:

lines.text: \Delta = 2\begin{vmatrix} a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b \end{vmatrix} = \text{R.H.S}

recall.must_convey: That −1 is taken out of row 2 and out of row 3, and that the two minus signs multiply to +1, leaving 2 times the required determinant.
accept: take minus one common from row two and row three and the two negatives cancel leaving two times the determinant
pull out minus one twice which gives plus one so only the two stays in front
the sign factors cancel and we get two into the determinant a b c b c a c a b
rendu rows nunchi minus one teeste minus signs cancel avthai, two matrame untundi
minus one from each of the two rows multiplies to one so the answer is twice the determinant

steps.why: Taking −1 out of a row is the same as taking any other common factor out of a row. Doing it twice puts (−1)(−1) in front, and that is 1 — so the sign disappears without any extra work.
common_mistakes: Taking −1 out of only one row and finishing with a negative answer.
Taking −1 out of the whole determinant instead of row by row.
Losing the 2 at the very last line.

insider_note: Add the rows into R₁ TWICE — once to bring out the 2, and again after the row subtractions to restore a, b, c. The two −1s taken out at the end cancel each other.
